challenge.method: Compare the three cited abstract sentences with the introduction, sections 2.2 and 2.3, and Parts III and IV. Test whether Prolog refers solely to the French dialogue application, an automated deduction system, Q-systems, or a single undifferentiated historic version. Compare the dates in the abstract against the narrative.
challenge.results: The first sentence distinguishes the language from the natural-language processing project. The introduction identifies Q-systems as a forerunner and distinguishes the two Prolog versions. Parts III and IV again describe preliminary then definitive Prolog. The abstract places the versions at the ends of 1971 and 1972, while the detailed sections describe preliminary Prolog in 1972 and definitive Prolog in 1973. The date discrepancy leaves the claimed language identity, version distinction and order intact. The claim expressly excludes exact genesis years and later ISO revisions.

limitations: Historical language identity as described by its early designers. The claim excludes exact genesis years and later ISO revisions.
The abstract and detailed narrative use differing years for the early versions. The assessment covers their identities and order.
